---
title: "Installation"
---

## Requirements

- PHP 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5, with the `mbstring` and `tokenizer` extensions. Most
  PHP builds include both, and Composer reports a missing one.
- Composer.
- Python 3 with the `venv` module. On Debian and Ubuntu that module is the
  `python3-venv` package.
- macOS or Linux.

The kernel runs in a Python environment with
[ipykernel](https://pypi.org/project/ipykernel/) 7.0 or later. The current
ipykernel release requires Python 3.11 or later. `juphyter install` uses an
existing environment that has ipykernel, or builds one.

Optional:

| Feature | Needed for |
|---|---|
| The `pcntl` PHP extension | Interrupting a running cell with the stop button. Without it the stop button does nothing. |
| [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) | Rendering `.qmd` documents. CI tests Quarto 1.10.18. |
| [vl-convert](https://github.com/vega/vl-convert/releases) | Static images of phiz plots in PDF and Word output. See [Output formats](quarto.qmd#output-formats). |
| phibble, phplyr, and phiz | Data frame tables and charts. See [The phpstats packages](#the-phpstats-packages). |

## Install juphyter

Install juphyter for your user and put Composer's bin directory on `PATH`:

```bash
composer global require phpstats/juphyter
export PATH="$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):$PATH"
```

## Register the kernel

```bash
juphyter install --create-venv ~/.venvs/juphyter
export PATH="$HOME/.venvs/juphyter/bin:$PATH"
```

- `juphyter install` registers a kernel named `php` for your user, so one
  install serves notebooks and documents in every directory.
- It uses the Python environment that owns the `jupyter` command on `PATH`
  when that environment has ipykernel. Otherwise it builds an environment with
  JupyterLab at the `--create-venv` path. It changes no existing Python
  installation.
- The kernel records absolute paths to the PHP binary, the Python
  interpreter, and juphyter. The PHP is the one running `juphyter install`,
  recorded as the first path on `PATH` that leads to it, such as
  `/opt/homebrew/bin/php`.
- The second `export` puts the environment first on `PATH`, so `jupyter lab`
  and `quarto render` find it. When `juphyter install` used an existing
  environment, the directory does not exist and the line has no effect.

The command prints the kernelspec, the PHP, the Python, and the engine it
recorded. When Quarto is installed and the Python Quarto would use has no
Jupyter, it also prints a warning with the `export` line that fixes it. The
kernel is still registered.

## Check the installation

```bash
juphyter doctor
```

`juphyter doctor` checks juphyter's files, the PHP that runs the cells, the
Python for the kernel, the Python Quarto will use, and every kernel juphyter
registered. It changes nothing, and it ends with two summary lines:

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `JupyterLab: ready, with php.` | The kernel is registered, and its PHP, Python, and juphyter files run. |
| `Quarto: ready.` | Quarto will run a Python that has Jupyter. |
| `Quarto: not installed.` | `quarto` is not on `PATH`. Quarto is needed only for rendering `.qmd` documents. |
| `Quarto: not ready.` | Quarto is installed and its Python lacks Jupyter or does not run. The report ends with the `export` line that fixes it. |

A line marked `fail` makes the command exit 1, and `Quarto: not ready.` is a
failure. A line marked `warn`, such as a missing `pcntl`, does not change the
exit code.

Run `juphyter doctor` again after upgrading PHP or Python, or after removing a
project or an environment. [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) covers the
failures it reports.

## Keeping the PATH entries

Both `export` lines last until the shell closes. To keep the `juphyter`
command in new shells, add Composer's bin directory to your shell startup
file. This appends to `~/.zshrc`. Use `~/.bashrc` for bash.

```bash
echo "export PATH=\"$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):\$PATH\"" >> ~/.zshrc
```

Putting the Python environment in a startup file makes it the `python3` for
every program, including every Quarto project on the machine.
[Python interpreters and editors](python.qmd) describes how to select it per
editor workspace, per shell, or per Quarto project instead.

## The phpstats packages

juphyter does not depend on phibble, phplyr, or phiz. A notebook inside a
Composer project that requires them can use them with the `php` kernel. To use
them in notebooks outside any project, install them globally and register a
second kernel that loads Composer's global autoloader:

```bash
composer global require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr phpstats/phiz
juphyter install --name phpstats --display-name "PHP (phpstats)" \
  --autoload "$(composer global config home)/vendor/autoload.php"
```

Documents name that kernel as `jupyter: phpstats`, and JupyterLab lists it as
"PHP (phpstats)". A kernel installed with `--autoload` always loads the
autoloader it names, even for a notebook inside a Composer project, which is
why it has its own name.

## Which classes a notebook sees

The kernel starts in the notebook's directory, looks upward for
`vendor/autoload.php`, and loads the first one it finds. A notebook anywhere
inside a Composer project can use that project's classes and packages.

Two settings replace that search. The more explicit one wins.

1. `JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD` in the kernel's environment. `juphyter install
   --autoload PATH` records it in the kernel.
2. A `juphyter.json` in the notebook's directory or any directory above it.

A `juphyter.json` can also set the memory limit and the include path:

```json
{
  "autoload": "vendor/autoload.php",
  "memory_limit": "512M",
  "include_path": "lib"
}
```

Relative paths resolve against the directory that holds `juphyter.json`.

## Installing into one project

juphyter can also be a development dependency of a project:

```bash
composer require --dev phpstats/juphyter
vendor/bin/juphyter install --name myproject
```

- The kernel is still registered for your user, and it runs that project's
  copy of juphyter.
- Without `--name`, a second project's install replaces the first project's
  `php` kernel, and the command reports it as `Replaced`.
- Deleting the project's `vendor` directory breaks the kernel, which
  `juphyter doctor` reports.

## Several PHP versions

Give each kernel its own name:

```bash
juphyter install --name php83 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.3/bin/php
juphyter install --name php85 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.5/bin/php
```

JupyterLab then lists "PHP 8.3" and "PHP 8.5". An absolute `--php` path is
recorded as written. A bare name such as `php8.4` is resolved to an absolute
path, because a kernel cannot rely on `PATH`.

## Where the kernel is registered

`juphyter install` writes a kernelspec, the `kernel.json` file Jupyter reads
to start a kernel, into the per-user Jupyter data directory. Every Jupyter
installation on the machine searches that directory.

| Platform | Directory |
|---|---|
| macOS | `~/Library/Jupyter/kernels` |
| Linux | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/jupyter/kernels`, or `~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels` |

`JUPYTER_DATA_DIR` replaces that directory, and `--prefix PATH` writes under
`PATH/share/jupyter` instead.

`juphyter uninstall --name NAME` removes a kernel that juphyter registered. It
refuses to remove a kernel of the same name that something else wrote, and so
does a reinstall.

## Options

`juphyter install --help` lists every option:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--name NAME` | The kernel's name, which documents use in `jupyter: NAME`. Default: `php`. |
| `--display-name TEXT` | The label JupyterLab shows. Default: the PHP version, such as `PHP 8.5`. |
| `--php PATH` | The PHP binary that runs cells. Default: the PHP running `juphyter install`. |
| `--python PATH` | The Python that hosts the kernel. Default: the one that owns `jupyter` on `PATH`. |
| `--prefix PATH` | Write under `PATH/share/jupyter`. |
| `--autoload PATH` | Load this autoloader instead of searching above the notebook. |
| `--create-venv PATH` | Where to build a Python environment when none can host the kernel. Without it, the command asks, and builds one at `~/.venvs/juphyter` when there is no terminal to ask. |

`juphyter --version` prints the installed version and the PHP running it.
